claim: HIV-1 Envelope (Env) variants are grouped into tiers by their neutralization-sensitivity phenotype.
source: HIV-1 Envelope (Env) variants are grouped into tiers by their neutralization-sensitivity phenotype.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as an established practice in the field.

claim: Tier 1 neutralization responses can be elicited readily, but do not protect against new infections.
source: This helped to recognize that tier 1 neutralization responses can be elicited readily, but do not protect against new infections.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction regarding vaccine trials.

claim: Tier 3 viruses are the least sensitive to neutralization.
source: Tier 3 viruses are the least sensitive to neutralization.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as an established characteristic.

claim: Most circulating viruses are tier 2.
source: Because most circulating viruses are tier 2, vaccines that elicit neutralization responses against them are needed.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Logistic regression of neutralization outcomes summarizes serum or antibody potency on a continuous, tier-like scale.
source: Logistic regression of neutralization outcomes summarizes serum or antibody potency on a continuous, tier-like scale.
evidence: This is the primary methodological claim of the manuscript, described in the abstract.

claim: The logistic regression method tests significance of the neutralization score to indicate cases where serum response does not depend on virus tiers.
source: It also tests significance of the neutralization score, to indicate cases where serum response does not depend on virus tiers.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a feature of the method.

claim: The method can standardize results from different virus panels.
source: The method can standardize results from different virus panels, and could lead to high-throughput assays, which evaluate a single serum dilution, rather than a dilution series, for more efficient use of limited resources to screen samples from vaccinees.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a capability of the method.

claim: The method could lead to high-throughput assays that evaluate a single serum dilution rather than a dilution series.
source: The method can standardize results from different virus panels, and could lead to high-throughput assays, which evaluate a single serum dilution, rather than a dilution series, for more efficient use of limited resources to screen samples from vaccinees.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a potential application.

claim: ID50 values are the inhibitory dilutions at which 50% neutralization is attained.
source: ID50 (or ID80) values, the inhibitory dilutions at which 50% (or 80%) neutralization is attained, are determined for a panel of viruses, using the TZM-bl neutralization assay (Sarzotti-Kelsoe et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a definition provided in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Serum breadth is the proportion of pseudoviruses with an ID50 score above the threshold of detection.
source: Breadth is the proportion of pseudoviruses with an ID50 score above the threshold of detection, and potency is the geometric mean ID50 (Hraber et al., 2014; Rademeyer et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a definition provided in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Serum potency is the geometric mean ID50.
source: Breadth is the proportion of pseudoviruses with an ID50 score above the threshold of detection, and potency is the geometric mean ID50 (Hraber et al., 2014; Rademeyer et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a definition provided in the introduction with citation support.

claim: At least half of the variation in neutralization assay results from large panels can be explained by the averaged responses per serum, Env, and the entire panel, overall.
source: At least half of the variation in neutralization assay results from large panels can be explained by the averaged responses per serum, Env, and the entire panel, overall (Hraber et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Serum breadth and potency depend strongly on the Env panels used, which can vary markedly between studies.
source: Serum breadth and potency therefore depend strongly on the Env panels used, which can vary markedly between studies.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an inference from the previous claim.

claim: Virus neutralization sensitivity to panels of sera from chronically infected individuals represents a continuum.
source: Virus neutralization sensitivity to panels of sera from chronically infected individuals represents a continuum (Seaman et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Characterizing Envs in tiers involves partitioning large neutralization panels into three or four groups with similar sensitivity.
source: To characterize Envs in tiers involves partitioning large neutralization panels into three or four groups with similar sensitivity (Rademeyer et al., 2016; Seaman et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Antibodies able to neutralize only tier 1 viruses are readily elicited by HIV Env gp120 immunogens.
source: Antibodies able to neutralize only tier 1 (most sensitive) viruses are readily elicited by HIV Env gp120 immunogens, but such tier1 responses are not protective; in human vaccine efficacy trials, such responses have been unable to confer protection against the viruses that continue to fuel the pandemic (Gilbert et al., 2010; Montefiori et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Tier 1 responses have been unable to confer protection against the viruses that continue to fuel the pandemic in human vaccine efficacy trials.
source: Antibodies able to neutralize only tier 1 (most sensitive) viruses are readily elicited by HIV Env gp120 immunogens, but such tier1 responses are not protective; in human vaccine efficacy trials, such responses have been unable to confer protection against the viruses that continue to fuel the pandemic (Gilbert et al., 2010; Montefiori et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Tier 2 viruses are more difficult to neutralize than tier 1.
source: Tier 2 viruses are more difficult to neutralize than tier 1, and represent the majority of viruses that are transmitted to establish new infections (Rademeyer et al., 2016; Seaman et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Tier 2 viruses represent the majority of viruses that are transmitted to establish new infections.
source: Tier 2 viruses are more difficult to neutralize than tier 1, and represent the majority of viruses that are transmitted to establish new infections (Rademeyer et al., 2016; Seaman et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: The tiered scheme for labeling viruses simplifies a continuous distribution into three or four categories.
source: One difficulty with the tiered scheme for labeling viruses (i.e. tiers 1A, 1B, 2, and 3) is that it simplifies a continuous distribution into three or four categories (Seaman et al., 2010), despite wide variation within each category.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a limitation of the current system.

claim: There is wide variation within each tier category.
source: One difficulty with the tiered scheme for labeling viruses (i.e. tiers 1A, 1B, 2, and 3) is that it simplifies a continuous distribution into three or four categories (Seaman et al., 2010), despite wide variation within each category.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a limitation of the current system.

claim: The tiered system categorizes viruses but does not help compare serum neutralization potency.
source: Moreover, while the system categorizes viruses, it does not help compare serum neutralization potency.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a limitation of the current system.

claim: The logarithm of the geometric mean ID50 against 205 sera was linearly rescaled to correspond with tier designations to assign neutralization index (NI) values to each HIV-1 envelope-pseudotyped virus.
source: The logarithm of the geometric mean ID50 against 205 sera was linearly rescaled to correspond with tier designations. The resulting NI values thus capture envelope neutralization sensitivity across 205 sera and provide a continuous scale of sensitivity that roughly corresponds to their tier designations.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the method.

claim: The resulting NI values capture envelope neutralization sensitivity across 205 sera and provide a continuous scale of sensitivity that roughly corresponds to their tier designations.
source: The resulting NI values thus capture envelope neutralization sensitivity across 205 sera and provide a continuous scale of sensitivity that roughly corresponds to their tier designations.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the method.

claim: The neutralization index could be defined in other ways, for example by using area-under-curve (AUC) values from the dilution series.
source: We note that the neutralization index could be defined in other ways, for example by using area-under-curve (AUC) values from the dilution series (Yu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an alternative approach with citation.

claim: The expectation for a typical serum is that it can more potently neutralize lower tier viruses than higher tier viruses.
source: As higher-tier viruses are more difficult to neutralize, the expectation for a typical serum is that it can more potently neutralize lower tier viruses than higher tier viruses.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a logical expectation.

claim: Serum neutralization potency (NP) is defined as the NI that gives equal probability for viruses sensitive and resistant to neutralization by that serum.
source: We define serum neutralization potency (NP) as the NI that gives equal probability for viruses sensitive and resistant to neutralization by that serum, which we estimate using logistic regression (Figure 1d and Materials and methods).
evidence: This is the key definition of the NP metric, stated in the Results section and illustrated in Figure 1d.

claim: Linear transformation of virus geometric mean ID50 neutralization titers provides a tiered scale based on previous reports.
source: Linear transformation of NSDP virus geometric mean ID50 neutralization titers provides a tiered scale, based on previous reports.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 2a caption and shown in the figure.

claim: Serum NPs are correlated with geometric mean ID50s per serum.
source: Serum NPs are correlated with geometric mean ID50s per serum but, because of the transformation applied to viruses, range from about 1 to 4, consistent with the established Env tier classification scheme.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 2b caption and shown in the figure.

claim: Serum NP values range from about 1 to 4, consistent with the established Env tier classification scheme.
source: Serum NPs are correlated with geometric mean ID50s per serum but, because of the transformation applied to viruses, range from about 1 to 4, consistent with the established Env tier classification scheme.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 2b caption and shown in the figure.

claim: Higher titers averaged across viruses indicate greater probability of neutralizing higher-tier, neutralization-resistant viruses.
source: Conversely for sera, higher titers averaged across viruses indicate greater probability of neutralizing higher-tier, neutralization-resistant viruses (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2b.

claim: Tier 3 sera (NP >3) are better able to neutralize tier 3 viruses than are tier 1 sera (NP <2).
source: That is, tier 3 sera (NP >3) are better able to neutralize tier 3 viruses than are tier 1 sera (NP <2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the NP metric.

claim: Low scatter gives a steep slope in logistic regression, indicating a sharp boundary between viruses neutralized and not neutralized.
source: Low scatter, as illustrated in Figure 1a and b, gives a steep slope in logistic regression, indicating a sharp boundary between viruses neutralized and not neutralized.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1.

claim: More scatter gives a lower slope, indicating lower contrast between viruses neutralized and not neutralized with increasing mean ID50.
source: More scatter, that is lower contrast between viruses neutralized and not neutralized with increasing mean ID50, as illustrated in Figure 1c, gives a lower slope.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1c.

claim: Inability to resolve between neutralization outcomes gives no slope, quantified by a high p-value from rejecting the null hypothesis that the slope is zero.
source: Inability to resolve between neutralization outcomes would give no slope, quantified by a high probability of a false positive (p value) from rejecting the null hypothesis that the slope is zero, as is true for some NP outcomes in Figure 2b.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2b.

claim: Inability to resolve between neutralization outcomes is most common at the low end of the serum neutralization continuum, where the ability to neutralize a virus is constant (and low) across the range of virus sensitivities.
source: This is most common at the low end of the serum neutralization continuum, where the ability to neutralize a virus is constant (and low) across the range of virus sensitivities.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation about when NP is poorly defined.

claim: NP values are robust to sampling variation, save for a few sera with a slope of zero.
source: Resampling (with replacement) sets of 225 Envs from the M group panel indicates that NP values are robust to sampling variation, save for a few sera with a slope of zero (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1a.

claim: Variation may increase slightly among resampled NP values at the extremes of the neutralization scale even when the slope is non-zero.
source: Variation may increase slightly among resampled NP values at the extremes of the neutralization scale even when the slope is non-zero (Figure 2—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Serum SA.C37 has median potency among the sera studied.
source: Neutralization responses for a typical serum, such as SA.C37, which has median potency among the sera we studied, appear in Figure 3.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the example serum.

claim: Serum SA.C37 has a neutralization potency of 2.5 computed from the 225 Env-panel.
source: Serum neutralization potency computed from the 225 Env-panel is 2.5.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3.

claim: Five Envs were shared by all three small panels (global, 10-Env lasso, and 20-Env lasso).
source: Together, five Envs were shared by all three small panels (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) and four additional Envs were common to both the global panel and 20-Env lasso panel, while the two hand-selected Envs were specific only to the global panel.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Four additional Envs were common to both the global panel and 20-Env lasso panel.
source: Together, five Envs were shared by all three small panels (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) and four additional Envs were common to both the global panel and 20-Env lasso panel, while the two hand-selected Envs were specific only to the global panel.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Two hand-selected Envs were specific only to the global panel.
source: Together, five Envs were shared by all three small panels (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) and four additional Envs were common to both the global panel and 20-Env lasso panel, while the two hand-selected Envs were specific only to the global panel.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Envs selected for smaller panels represent a range of neutralization sensitivities, favoring more sensitive and disfavoring the insensitive viruses.
source: The Envs that were selected to infer NP from smaller panels represent a range of neutralization sensitivities, favoring more sensitive and disfavoring the insensitive viruses (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The 20-Env panel is better able to resolve between neutralization outcomes (p=0.000162) than smaller panels for serum SA.C37.
source: A review of the ability of each panel to model NP for the serum SA.C37 (Figure 4) suggests that the 20-Env panel, as might be expected, is better able to resolve between neutralization outcomes (p=0.000162, Figure 4c) than smaller panels (Figure 4a and b; p=0.00298 and p=0.00151 for global and 10-Env panels, respectively).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 4 and specific p-values.

claim: The standard global panel performed as well as the lasso panel of 10 for serum SA.C37.
source: In this example, the standard global panel performed as well as the lasso panel of 10.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section comparing the panels.

claim: NP values inferred from smaller panels are correlated with NP values from larger sets of holdout, non-panel Envs.
source: NP values inferred from smaller panels are correlated with NP values from larger sets of holdout, non-panel Envs, and also with each other, across panels (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The lasso-selected panel of 10 and the global panel perform similarly.
source: The lasso-selected panel of 10 and the global panel perform similarly, so the global panel performs reasonably well for a panel of that size.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section comparing panel performance.

claim: The global panel may offer greater resolution for tier 1A and 1B sera because it includes more Envs with NI below 2.0 than either of the panels selected by lasso.
source: The global panel may offer greater resolution for tier 1A and 1B sera, because it includes more Envs with NI below 2.0 than either of the panels selected by lasso.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a potential advantage of the global panel.

claim: With panel Envs, inferred serum NP values were roughly limited to range from 1 to 4.
source: With panel Envs, inferred serum NP values were roughly limited to range from 1 to 4.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the range of NP values.

claim: When more Envs are tested, the NP values can fall below 1 or above 4, most likely because the most extreme Envs on the neutralization continuum allow the logistic regression to fit parameters outside the range typically expected.
source: When more Envs are tested, the NP values can fall below 1 or above 4, most likely because the most extreme Envs on the neutralization continuum allow the logistic regression to fit parameters outside the range typically expected.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section explaining why NP values can exceed the expected range.

claim: The 20-Env panel is better powered to detect a non-zero slope than the smaller 10- and 11-Env panels over all 205 sera.
source: Over all the 205 sera, the 20-Env panel is better powered to detect a non-zero slope than the smaller 10- and 11-Env panels (Figure 4—figure supplement 3), giving p>0.05 in about half as many cases as the smaller panels, likely because greater statistical power results from having nearly twice as many measurements to compute logistic regression parameters.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: The 20-Env panel gives p>0.05 in about half as many cases as the smaller panels.
source: Over all the 205 sera, the 20-Env panel is better powered to detect a non-zero slope than the smaller 10- and 11-Env panels (Figure 4—figure supplement 3), giving p>0.05 in about half as many cases as the smaller panels, likely because greater statistical power results from having nearly twice as many measurements to compute logistic regression parameters.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: Greater statistical power results from having nearly twice as many measurements to compute logistic regression parameters.
source: Over all the 205 sera, the 20-Env panel is better powered to detect a non-zero slope than the smaller 10- and 11-Env panels (Figure 4—figure supplement 3), giving p>0.05 in about half as many cases as the smaller panels, likely because greater statistical power results from having nearly twice as many measurements to compute logistic regression parameters.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an explanation for the better performance of the 20-Env panel.

claim: NP can be computed using a reasonable choice of Envs that represent a range of neutralization sensitivities.
source: Overall, rather than recommending use of a single panel to compute NP, it seems NP can be computed using a reasonable choice of Envs that represent a range of neutralization sensitivities, and use of more Envs is better able to quantify NP significantly than fewer Envs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion about panel selection.

claim: Use of more Envs is better able to quantify NP significantly than fewer Envs.
source: Overall, rather than recommending use of a single panel to compute NP, it seems NP can be computed using a reasonable choice of Envs that represent a range of neutralization sensitivities, and use of more Envs is better able to quantify NP significantly than fewer Envs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion about panel size.

claim: 25 of 103 donor sera were previously found to be long-term non-progressors (LTNP).
source: Using previously reported neutralization assay results (Doria-Rose et al., 2010), we computed geometric mean ID50 titers from 20 Envs and 103 donor sera, of which 25 were previously found to be long-term non-progressors (LTNP) (Migueles et al., 2002; Migueles et al., 2008; Doria-Rose et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation support.

claim: Ten Envs in the LTNP panel were also tested in the M group panel.
source: We identified 10 Envs in this panel that were also tested in the M group panel, two from subtype C (DU422.1, DU156.12), seven from subtype B (BG1168.1, 6101.10, TRJO4551.58, PVO.4, CAAN5342.A2, THRO4156.18, TRO.11), and one from subtype A (Q769.D22).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the overlap between panels.

claim: A p-value cutoff of 0.1 from χ2 testing was used to indicate a significant NP score in the LTNP analysis.
source: We computed NP values from these 10 Envs, using a cutoff ID50 of 50 for positive neutralization outcome, and p-value cutoff from χ2 testing of 0.1 to indicate a significant NP score.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the analysis parameters.

claim: The p-value cutoff excluded 4 of 25 LTNP sera and 20 of 78 progressors.
source: This cutoff excluded 4 of 25 LTNP sera and 20 of 78 progressors; the proportions of excluded NP values were not significantly different between progressors and non-progressors (Fisher's exact test, p=0.42).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with statistical test results.

claim: The proportions of excluded NP values were not significantly different between progressors and non-progressors (Fisher's exact test, p=0.42).
source: This cutoff excluded 4 of 25 LTNP sera and 20 of 78 progressors; the proportions of excluded NP values were not significantly different between progressors and non-progressors (Fisher's exact test, p=0.42).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with statistical test results.

claim: NP values are highly correlated with geometric mean ID50s (Kendall's τ, p<2.2 × 10−16) in the LTNP analysis.
source: NP values are highly correlated with geometric mean ID50s (Figure 5), regardless of whether or not NP outcomes with high p-values from χ2 testing are excluded (Kendall's τ, p<2.2 × 10−16).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5 and statistical test results.

claim: The geometric mean ID50s differed significantly between the progressors and non-progressors (Wilcoxon test, p=2.1 × 10−11).
source: As anticipated, based on the established studies (Doria-Rose et al., 2010), the geometric mean ID50s differed significantly between the progressors and non-progressors (Wilcoxon test, p=2.1 × 10−11).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with statistical test results and citation.

claim: Breadth, defined as the percentage of 20 Envs neutralized per serum with an ID50 of at least 50, differed significantly between progressors and non-progressors (Wilcoxon p=7.2 × 10−11).
source: We noted the same outcome for breadth, defined as the percentage of 20 Envs neutralized per serum with an ID50 of at least 50 (Wilcoxon p=7.2 × 10−11).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with statistical test results.

claim: NP values differed significantly between progressors and non-progressors (n = 79, Wilcoxon p=4.3 × 10−9).
source: Similarly, NP values differed significantly between these groups (n = 79, Wilcoxon p=4.3 × 10−9).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with statistical test results.

claim: The NP comparison agrees with established findings but involves half as many Envs and could use many fewer dilutions than required to compute mean ID50s among 20 Envs.
source: This NP comparison therefore agrees with established findings (Doria-Rose et al., 2010), but notably, the NP comparisons involved half as many Envs and could use many fewer dilutions than required to compute mean ID50s among 20 Envs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section comparing the efficiency of the NP method.

claim: To repeat the NP analysis using single-dilution assays, the entire comparison would require at most one-tenth the number of neutralization reactions and material per sample compared with the experiment using mean ID50 titers.
source: To repeat the NP analysis using single-dilution assays, rather than a five-point (or greater) dilution series, the entire comparison would require at most one-tenth the number of neutralization reactions and material per sample, compared with the experiment using mean ID50 titers.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the efficiency advantage of the NP method.

claim: Testing more than 10 Envs per serum could increase statistical power and reduce the number of sera excluded because their NP scores were deemed insufficiently significant.
source: Also, as seen above, testing more than 10 Envs per serum could increase statistical power, and reduce the number of sera excluded because their NP scores were deemed insufficiently significant.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a recommendation for improving the method.

claim: Recent work has introduced mutations to stabilize the clade A BG505 SOSIP.664 trimer and reduce conformational changes in the CD4-bound state.
source: Recent work to stabilize the clade A BG505 SOSIP.664 trimer and reduce conformational changes in the CD4-bound state has introduced mutations that increase hydrophobic packing of the V3 loop region, increase sensitivity to known neutralizing antibodies, and add disulfide bonds between gp120 and gp41 subunits within or between protomers. (Sanders et al., 2013; Pugach et al., 2015; Julien et al., 2015; de Taeye et al., 2015; Ringe et al., 2017)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with multiple citations.

claim: These mutations increase hydrophobic packing of the V3 loop region, increase sensitivity to known neutralizing antibodies, and add disulfide bonds between gp120 and gp41 subunits within or between protomers.
source: Recent work to stabilize the clade A BG505 SOSIP.664 trimer and reduce conformational changes in the CD4-bound state has introduced mutations that increase hydrophobic packing of the V3 loop region, increase sensitivity to known neutralizing antibodies, and add disulfide bonds between gp120 and gp41 subunits within or between protomers. (Sanders et al., 2013; Pugach et al., 2015; Julien et al., 2015; de Taeye et al., 2015; Ringe et al., 2017)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with multiple citations.

claim: These mutations have been introduced to several Env isolates in addition to BG505, including a C-clade Env, ZM197M, to demonstrate general suitability of the approach.
source: These mutations have been introduced to several Env isolates in addition to BG505, including a C-clade Env, ZM197M, to demonstrate general suitability of the approach (Pugach et al., 2015; Julien et al., 2015; de Taeye et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: A recent study evaluated antigenicity and immunogenicity of next-generation modified SOSIP trimers, designated v4 through v6.
source: A recent study (Torrents de la Peña et al., 2017) evaluated antigenicity and immunogenicity of these next-generation modified SOSIP trimers, designated v4 through v6.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation.

claim: Post-vaccination serological data was analyzed from 50 rabbits sampled 22 weeks after the first vaccination (boosted at weeks 4 and 20).
source: We analyzed the post-vaccination serological data by computing neutralization potency scores from ID50 neutralization titers in 50 rabbits sampled 22 weeks after the first vaccination (boosted at weeks 4 and 20).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the analysis.

claim: Fifteen viruses from the SOSIP trimer study overlapped with the set for which NI values were already computed.
source: Fifteen viruses from that study overlapped with the set for which we have already computed NI values, which we tabulate from most to least sensitive (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Table 1.

claim: All but two of 50 rabbits tested yielded p-values below 0.05 using a cutoff ID50 of 50.
source: Results complement the original findings, and add to interpretation of the original assay results. Using a cutoff ID50 of 50, all but two of 50 rabbits tested yielded p-values below 0.05 (Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Table 2.

claim: Two animals (1586 and 1591 from Study C022-15, vaccinated with BG505 SOSIP.v5.1 and BG505 SOSIP.v5.2, respectively) neutralized only WITO, which is a relatively resistant Env.
source: These two animals (1586 and 1591 from Study C022-15, vaccinated with BG505 SOSIP.v5.1 and BG505 SOSIP.v5.2, respectively) neutralized only WITO, which is a relatively resistant Env.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing specific animals.

claim: Animals 1586 and 1591 had lower and questionable NP values (NP = 0.87, χ2 p=0.0831 for both) compared to animal 1588 (NP = 1.73, χ2 p=0.0171), despite similar breadth and potency.
source: Comparing animals that showed similar breadth (7%, or 1 of 15 Envs neutralized) and potency (geometric mean ID50 of 13.3 and 12.8, respectively), the NP values from animals 1586 and 1591 are lower and of questionable significance (NP = 0.87, χ2 p=0.0831 for both) than animal 1588, vaccinated with BG505 SOSIP.v5.1 (NP = 1.73, χ2 p=0.0171).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section comparing specific animals.

claim: In Study C0120-15, three of five animals vaccinated with ZM197M SOSIP.v5.2 (IDs 1875, 1876, and 1878) showed 20% breadth, geometric mean titers of 19.3, 19.1, and 21.9, and NP values above 2.0, with χ2 p-values below 0.05.
source: Similarly, comparing outcomes in Study C0120-15 (Table 2), three of five animals vaccinated with ZM197M SOSIP.v5.2 (with IDs of 1875, 1876, and 1878) showed 20% breadth (3 of 15 Envs neutralized), geometric mean titers of 19.3, 19.1, and 21.9, and NP values above 2.0, with χ2 p-values below 0.05.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Table 2.

claim: The ZM197M SOSIP.v5.2 immunogen induced tier 2 responses in 4 of 5 rabbits and yielded the most promising outcome among the refined SOSIP immunogens studied.
source: This immunogen induced tier 2 responses in 4 of 5 rabbits, and yielded the most promising outcome among the refined SOSIP immunogens studied, though the clade-A BG505 trimers may have been at disadvantage because there were fewer clade-A Envs and A-related recombinants in the set utilized than clade-C Envs and C-related recombinants (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Table 1.

claim: The clade-A BG505 trimers may have been at disadvantage because there were fewer clade-A Envs and A-related recombinants in the set utilized than clade-C Envs and C-related recombinants.
source: This immunogen induced tier 2 responses in 4 of 5 rabbits, and yielded the most promising outcome among the refined SOSIP immunogens studied, though the clade-A BG505 trimers may have been at disadvantage because there were fewer clade-A Envs and A-related recombinants in the set utilized than clade-C Envs and C-related recombinants (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a caveat about the comparison.

claim: NP analysis agreed with the other neutralization metrics considered and was able to resolve apparent ties between animals with similar neutralization responses to different Envs.
source: NP analysis agreed with the other neutralization metrics considered, and was able to resolve apparent ties between animals with similar neutralization responses to different Envs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion about the NP method.

claim: The NP and slope of the logistic function increase as bnAbs are combined in most cases, but not all.
source: The NP and also the slope of the logistic function increase as bnAbs are combined in most cases, but not all (Figure 6).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6.

claim: Sera with higher number of antibody specificities could have higher NP and slope values.
source: These results suggest that, all else equal, sera with higher number of antibody specificities could have higher NP and slope values.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the antibody combination data.

claim: The NP statistic defines the greatest virus tier that a serum can be expected to neutralize.
source: The NP statistic defines the greatest virus tier that a serum can be expected to neutralize.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the NP metric.

claim: An NP of (roughly) 1.8 to 2.8 is 'tier 2-like', and an NP above 2.8 is 'tier 3-like'.
source: Thus, an NP of (roughly) 1.8 to 2.8 is 'tier 2-like', and an NP above 2.8 is 'tier 3-like'.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation guideline.

claim: NP values below 1 are unable to neutralize even tier 1A Envs.
source: NP values below 1 are unable to neutralize even tier 1A Envs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation guideline.

claim: The NP values are not absolute and depend on the ID50 cutoff used.
source: The NP values are not absolute and depend on the ID50 cutoff used.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a caveat about the NP metric.

claim: Defining a neutralization potency by testing a serum against a panel of 225 Envs on a routine basis is impractical and costly.
source: Defining a neutralization potency by testing a serum against a panel of 225 Envs on a routine basis is impractical and costly.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a practical limitation.

claim: Subsets of Envs were identified that largely reproduce the results from testing all 225 Envs.
source: We identified subsets of these Envs that largely reproduce the results from testing all 225.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section summarizing the panel selection work.

claim: The already established 12-virus global panel may suffice to characterize NP values, although larger panels tend to give more significant outcomes.
source: The already established 12-virus global panel may suffice to characterize NP values, although larger panels tend to give more significant outcomes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a recommendation.

claim: Evaluating neutralization assay outcomes against the continuum of neutralization sensitivity among viral variants provides more context to interpret results.
source: Evaluating neutralization assay outcomes against the continuum of neutralization sensitivity among viral variants provides more context to interpret results, because it considers not only the proportion of tier 2 Envs neutralized (breadth), but which Envs should most likely be neutralized.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an advantage of the method.

claim: The NP method helps to interpret differences between sera that neutralize the same number of Envs, each of which have different sensitivities.
source: This helps to interpret differences between sera that neutralize the same number of Envs, each of which have different sensitivities.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an advantage of the method.

claim: The NP method helps to compare sera where titers may be averaged over many outcomes below the limit of assay quantification.
source: It also helps to compare sera where titers may be averaged over many outcomes below the limit of assay quantification, as was the case for sera from vaccinated rabbits (Table 2) (Torrents de la Peña et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with reference to Table 2 and citation.

claim: Results from experiments that utilized different Env panels can be compared on the same neutralization scale.
source: We also explored results from experiments that utilized different Env panels and found they can be compared on the same neutralization scale (not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a finding.

claim: The ability to compare different Env panels requires only that some number of Envs in each panel have available tiered neutralization scores, computed from available data.
source: The ability to do this requires only that some number of Envs in each panel have available tiered neutralization scores, computed from available data.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a requirement for the method.

claim: Better comparative results are obtained when using more Envs, because resulting NP values are less likely to be undefined.
source: Better comparative results are obtained when using more Envs, because resulting NP values are less likely to be undefined.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a recommendation.

claim: A web-based utility at the Los Alamos HIV database computes NPs for sera tested against subsets of M group Envs.
source: A web-based utility – http://hiv.lanl.gov/content/sequence/NI/ni.html – at the Los Alamos HIV database computes NPs for sera tested against subsets of M group Envs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section describing a resource.

claim: The web-based utility can compute and report NPs for clade C Envs and for antibody IC50s.
source: In addition to the analysis described here, it can also compute and report NPs for clade C Envs (Rademeyer et al., 2016) and for antibody IC50s.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section describing the utility's capabilities.

claim: The same analytic methods can be applied to IC50s from antibodies.
source: We applied the same analytic methods to IC50s from antibodies.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section describing the method's applicability.

claim: Analysis of data from experiments that combined broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) having distinct specificities suggests that the NP increases with the number or variety of distinct antibody specificities in the sample.
source: Our analysis of data from experiments that combined broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) having distinct specificities suggests that the NP increases with the number or variety of distinct antibody specificities in the sample.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a finding from the antibody combination analysis.

claim: The slope indicates agreement between serum neutralization outcomes and average potency (geometric mean ID50) among serum samples used to compute the NI per Env.
source: The slope indicates agreement between serum neutralization outcomes and average potency (geometric mean ID50) among serum samples used to compute the NI per Env.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the slope parameter.

claim: The slope should be low for sera with limited epitope breadth.
source: We hypothesize that the slope should be low for sera with limited epitope breadth.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a hypothesis.

claim: In the extreme case of a serum that targets a single epitope, only Envs with that epitope would be neutralized, and neutralization outcomes should be widely scattered among viruses tested, independent of an overall sensitivity of the virus to neutralization, resulting in a slope near zero.
source: In the extreme case of a serum that targets a single epitope (e.g. a monoclonal response dominates), only Envs with that epitope would be neutralized, and neutralization outcomes should be widely scattered among viruses tested, independent of an overall sensitivity of the virus to neutralization, resulting in a slope near zero.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a theoretical prediction.

claim: The slope may indicate diversity of epitopes targeted by the test serum.
source: Thus, the slope may indicate diversity of epitopes targeted by the test serum.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a hypothesis.

claim: Single monoclonal bnAbs had lower slopes than mixtures of monoclonal bnAbs.
source: Consistent with this, we found single monoclonal bnAbs had lower slopes than mixtures of monoclonal bnAbs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a finding supporting the hypothesis about slope.

claim: The slope finding might help characterize the mixtures of antibody specificities in polyclonal sera, to complement the methods for computational neutralization fingerprinting.
source: Such a finding might help characterize the mixtures of antibody specificities in polyclonal sera, to complement the methods for computational neutralization fingerprinting that have recently been advanced (Georgiev et al., 2013; Doria-Rose et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a potential application with citations.

claim: A primary advantage of this approach is that it suggests a strategy to simplify neutralization assay experiments for more cost-effective screening of responses in large-scale vaccination studies.
source: In addition to establishing a metric for serum neutralization, a primary advantage of this approach is that it suggests a strategy to simplify neutralization assay experiments, for more cost-effective screening of responses in large-scale vaccination studies.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an advantage of the method.

claim: Logistic regression utilizes a collection of binary ('true' or 'false') responses, rather than the actual neutralization titers.
source: Logistic regression utilizes a collection of binary ('true' or 'false') responses, rather than the actual neutralization titers.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section describing the method.

claim: The logistic regression derivation relies only on a single-dilution analysis, rather than the current eight-point dilution series, enabling a larger-scale screening throughput.
source: Because its derivation relies only on a single-dilution analysis, rather than the current eight-point dilution series, it can enable a larger-scale screening throughput.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an advantage of the method.

claim: Sera that score well using the NP screening metric could be prioritized for a more thorough dilution-series analysis.
source: Sera that score well using this screening metric could be prioritized for a more thorough dilution-series analysis.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a potential application.

claim: The slope (which may indicate breadth of epitopes targeted) together with NP could be useful to down-select vaccine candidates and move forward with regimens that are able to elicit, on average, greater NP values.
source: Together with the slope (which may indicate breadth of epitopes targeted), this approach could be useful to down-select vaccine candidates and move forward with regimens that are able to elicit, on average, greater NP values.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a potential application.

claim: The greatest geometric mean ID50 against tier 3 Envs was 26.7 in an earlier study.
source: In an earlier study that inferred tiers using Envs and unpooled sera (Rademeyer et al., 2016), the greatest geometric mean ID50 against tier 3 Envs was 26.7 and the greatest geometric mean ID50 against tier 2 Envs was 117.6.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with citation.

claim: The greatest geometric mean ID50 against tier 2 Envs was 117.6 in an earlier study.
source: In an earlier study that inferred tiers using Envs and unpooled sera (Rademeyer et al., 2016), the greatest geometric mean ID50 against tier 3 Envs was 26.7 and the greatest geometric mean ID50 against tier 2 Envs was 117.6.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with citation.

claim: These two values (26.7 and 117.6) were used to set the boundaries between tiers 2 and 3 and between tiers 1 and 2, respectively.
source: We used these two values to set the boundaries between tiers 2 and 3 and between tiers 1 and 2, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing the transformation.

claim: The NI was computed from Env geometric mean ID50s as 2 – [log(geometric mean ID50) – log(117.6)] / [log(117.6) – log(26.7)].
source: We call this single transformed value for each virus the neutralization index (NI), and computed NI from Env geometric mean ID50s as 2 – [log(geometric mean ID50) – log(117.6)] / [log(117.6) – log(26.7)].
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section providing the formula.

claim: The NI is a continuously valued quantity, which can be interpreted intuitively on the tier scale.
source: The NI is a continuously valued quantity, which can be interpreted intuitively on the tier scale, for example tier 1 viruses have higher mean neutralization ID50s and lower NI than tier 3 viruses.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing the NI.

claim: Any linear transformation of the log-transformed geometric mean ID50s would yield results identical to the findings, but on a modified numerical scale.
source: Any linear transformation of the log-transformed geometric mean ID50s, or leaving them as they stand, would yield results identical to our findings, but on a modified numerical scale.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section as a note about the transformation.

claim: The NI transformation makes it possible to interpret neutralization scores in terms of the familiar tier system.
source: The NI transformation makes it possible to interpret neutralization scores in terms of the familiar tier system.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section as the purpose of the transformation.

claim: In a vaccine setting, a more generous cutoff (say 1:20) might be desirable.
source: While 1:50 is a good working choice for sera from natural infection cases, in a vaccine setting, a more generous choice (say 1:20) might be desirable.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section as a suggestion for alternative cutoffs.

claim: The M group neutralization data have a median ID50 of 28, and 37% of observations are above the 1:50 cutoff value.
source: The M group neutralization data (Hraber et al., 2014) have a median ID50 of 28, and 37% of observations are above the 1:50 cutoff value.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with citation.

claim: Logistic regression was used to model the probability of neutralization as a function of the tier-transformed virus neutralization score (NI), using the glm function in R (version 3.4.0).
source: For each serum, we use logistic regression to model the probability of neutralization as a function of the tier-transformed virus neutralization score (NI), using the glm function in R (version 3.4.0).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing the analysis.

claim: In cases where parameter estimation did not converge on a solution, the function glm2 (version 1.1.2) was used with more iterations to ensure optimization converges on the solution.
source: In cases where parameter estimation did not converge on a solution, we used the function glm2 (version 1.1.2) and more iterations, to ensure optimization converges on the solution. The glm2 function was designed to overcome the convergence limitations of its predecessor (Marschner, 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with citation.

claim: The logistic function is defined as p(x)=1/[1 + exp(b0 + b1 x)], with x the independent variable, and two parameters: intercept (b0) and slope (b1).
source: The logistic function is defined as p(x)=1/[1 + exp(b0 + b1 x)], with x the independent variable, and two parameters: intercept (b0) and slope (b1).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section defining the logistic function.

claim: Neutralization potency (NP) is defined as –b0/b1, which corresponds to the NI that has equal odds of being neutralized or not.
source: We define neutralization potency (NP) as –b0/b1. This corresponds to the NI that has equal odds of being neutralized or not (Crawley, 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with citation.

claim: Two hypothetical viruses with extreme phenotypes were included: one always sensitive to neutralization by any serum with a tiered score of 0, and one always resistant to neutralization with a tiered score of 5.
source: In practice, we found it useful to include two hypothetical viruses with extreme phenotypes, one always sensitive to neutralization by any serum, with a tiered score of 0, and one always resistant to neutralization, with a tiered score of 5.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing the analysis procedure.

claim: These extreme hypothetical viruses help to define the NP and ensure the regression calculations perform as expected.
source: These extremes help to define the NP and ensure the regression calculations perform as expected.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section explaining the purpose of the hypothetical viruses.

claim: NP is undefined if the slope is zero because it would require division by zero.
source: An important caveat remains to be addressed. Because it would require division by zero, NP is undefined if the slope is zero.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section as a limitation.

claim: A slope of zero occurs when the probability of neutralization is independent of the tier-transformed NI values for viruses.
source: This occurs when the probability of neutralization is independent of the tier-transformed NI values for viruses (i.e. is a constant equal to the breadth of the serum), meaning there is no consistent NI value that can separate neutralized from non-neutralized viruses.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section explaining when slope is zero.

claim: A slope of zero might result in cases of low statistical power, a non-representative selection of viruses, or a serum with a response that is otherwise atypical of sera used to compute mean virus neutralization titers.
source: This might result in cases of low statistical power, a non-representative selection of viruses (they are assumed random and independent), or a serum with a response that is otherwise atypical of sera used to compute mean virus neutralization titers.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section explaining causes of zero slope.

claim: A likelihood-ratio test computes a p-value from the χ2 distribution for the reduction in deviance that results from adding a slope to the regression model.
source: Because the slope is a statistical inference, a formalism exists to evaluate the null hypothesis of no slope. This is achieved by a likelihood-ratio test, which computes a p-value from the χ2 distribution for the reduction in deviance that results from adding a slope to the regression model (Crawley, 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with citation.

claim: A small p-value indicates a significant, non-zero slope, and that the NP is well defined.
source: A small p-value indicates a significant, non-zero slope, and that the NP is well defined.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section explaining p-value interpretation.

claim: NP values with high p-values should be interpreted with caution.
source: NP values with high p-values should be interpreted with caution.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section as a recommendation.

claim: A global panel of 12 viruses was developed for its ability to model the median of the distribution of the magnitude-breadth curve.
source: Recently a global panel of 12 viruses was developed for its ability to model the median of the distribution of the magnitude-breadth curve (deCamp et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with citation.

claim: The global panel was selected using lasso to identify nine Envs for their ability to model the median area under the dilution-series curve (AUC) for many sera.
source: That panel was selected using lasso to identify nine Envs for their ability to model the median area under the dilution-series curve (AUC) for many sera.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing the global panel.

claim: Three Envs were added manually to the global panel to include some neutralization response profiles not included in the nine.
source: To these Envs, three were added manually, to include some neutralization response profiles not included in the nine.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing the global panel.

claim: One virus (clade A, 398-F1_F6_20) was omitted from the global panel because it was missing values from 39 of 205 sera.
source: Because of missing values among the NSDP panel data, we omitted one virus (clade A, 398-F1_F6_20), which was missing values from 39 of 205 sera.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section explaining the panel modification.

claim: The virus was omitted because the missing value would have caused different effective sample sizes across sera and may have reduced the apparent robustness of resulting NP values.
source: We did this because the missing value would have caused different effective sample sizes across sera and may have reduced the apparent robustness of resulting NP values.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section explaining the rationale for omission.

claim: Lasso was used to select alternative small panels to model the logarithm of the geometric mean ID50 per serum.
source: Because our approach to compute NP values uses mean ID50 as an input variable, we again used lasso (Tibshirani, 1996) to select alternative small panels. Here, instead of modeling median AUC, we sought predictors to model the logarithm of the geometric mean ID50 per serum, using the glmnet R package(Friedman et al., 2010), version 2.0–10, to obtain panels of 10 and 20 Envs.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with citations.

claim: Lasso identified 10 Envs that explained 47.2% of the deviance that would be explained by a fully saturated model.
source: Lasso identified 10 Envs that explained 47.2% of the deviance that would be explained by a fully saturated model (the maximum-likelihood solution, involving all Envs) and 20 Envs explained 80.8% of the deviance.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 4—figure supplement 1 caption.

claim: 20 Envs explained 80.8% of the deviance that would be explained by a fully saturated model.
source: Lasso identified 10 Envs that explained 47.2% of the deviance that would be explained by a fully saturated model (the maximum-likelihood solution, involving all Envs) and 20 Envs explained 80.8% of the deviance.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 4—figure supplement 1 caption.

claim: Bootstrap resampling (with replacement) was used to assess NP robustness.
source: We used bootstrap resampling (with replacement) to assess NP robustness, and summarized the results as median and inter-quartile range per serum.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing the validation approach.

claim: Panel robustness was evaluated by comparing the NP values from the panel and the remaining held-out Envs, testing for correlations between them.
source: To evaluate panel robustness, we compare the NP values from the panel and the remaining held-out Envs, testing for correlations between them.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing the validation approach.
